_doc: CHANGE-1 (Rowan, 2026-11-22: 'humans are always the weak link in these information-to-action pipelines ... use the best of evidence-based behavioral psychology to inform and prompt real change'). The library of evidence-based moves an Ultrastable app uses to carry a person from a fact to a changed belief to an action. Every DEPTH-1 idea names at least min_per_idea of these in its `change` field; foundation/ideas.py depth() refuses an idea that names fewer or names one not in this library. Each method credits its source. Evidence strength is the literature's, stated plainly; a method with mixed evidence says so.

guess-first.move: ask the person to predict before the reveal, so the gap between guess and fact is felt (prediction error)
guess-first.source: Pan, S.C. and Rickard, T.C. (2018), Transfer of test-enhanced learning, Psychological Bulletin; Kornell, Hays and Bjork (2009) on pretesting

why-it-feels-true.move: start from why the intuition is reasonable before correcting it, so the reader is not put on the defensive
why-it-feels-true.source: Lewandowsky, Ecker et al. (2020), The Debunking Handbook 2020

fact-myth-fallacy.move: lead with the fact, name the myth once, explain the fallacy, repeat the fact (the truth sandwich)
fact-myth-fallacy.source: Lewandowsky, Ecker et al. (2020), The Debunking Handbook 2020

self-affirmation.move: let the person affirm a value they hold before meeting threatening evidence, which lowers defensive rejection
self-affirmation.source: Cohen, G.L. and Sherman, D.K. (2014), The psychology of change: self-affirmation and social psychological intervention, Annual Review of Psychology

consider-the-opposite.move: prompt the person to argue the other side or list reasons they could be wrong
consider-the-opposite.source: Lord, Lepper and Preston (1984), Considering the opposite: a corrective strategy for social judgment, JPSP

outside-view.move: show the reference class and its base rate before the specific case
outside-view.source: Kahneman and Lovallo (1993), Timid choices and bold forecasts; Flyvbjerg (2006), From Nobel Prize to project management

prebunking.move: warn of a misleading technique and show a weakened example before the person meets it (inoculation)
prebunking.source: van der Linden et al. (2017), Inoculating the public against misinformation about climate change, Global Challenges; Roozenbeek et al. (2022), Science Advances

graded-uncertainty.move: grade every source by study design and show the grade, including where the evidence is weak
graded-uncertainty.source: GRADE Working Group, Guyatt et al. (2008), BMJ

implementation-intention.move: turn the insight into an if-then plan: when situation X happens, I will do Y
implementation-intention.source: Gollwitzer, P.M. and Sheeran, P. (2006), Implementation intentions and goal achievement: a meta-analysis, Advances in Experimental Social Psychology

easy-attractive-social-timely.move: make the next step easy, attractive, social and timely (one tap, at the moment it applies)
easy-attractive-social-timely.source: Behavioural Insights Team (2014), EAST: four simple ways to apply behavioural insights

com-b.move: check capability, opportunity and motivation for the action and remove the missing one
com-b.source: Michie, van Stralen and West (2011), The behaviour change wheel, Implementation Science

social-norms.move: show what most people like the reader actually do or believe, when the true norm is the better behaviour
social-norms.source: Cialdini, Reno and Kallgren (1990), A focus theory of normative conduct, JPSP

spaced-follow-up.move: come back at spaced intervals (for example 7 and 14 days) to retrieve the idea and check the action
spaced-follow-up.source: Cepeda et al. (2006), Distributed practice in verbal recall tasks, Psychological Bulletin

calibration-feedback.move: keep the person's own record of guesses against outcomes, so updating becomes a habit
calibration-feedback.source: Tetlock and Gardner (2015), Superforecasting; Mellers et al. (2014), Psychological Science

change-management.move: for someone carrying the change into a team or institution: name the people affected, a small first win, and how to reinforce it
change-management.source: Kotter (1996), Leading Change; Michie et al. (2011) for the behavioural layer
